correctness.rationale: The source proves that the cone is Gorenstein, its resolution is smooth and an isomorphism off the vertex, its vertex has minimal log discrepancy zero, the lifted cyclic action is free, the product action is virtually free, the quotient preserves closed-point minimal log discrepancies, and the origin of X_m has minimal log discrepancy one and canonical index m. For m at least 2 the diagonal action has trivial stabilizer at every point except (0_Y,0): off the vertex this follows from freeness on the equivariant resolution, and over the vertex it follows from the nontrivial scalar action on t. Hence the quotient is étale away from the origin. Regularity and Gorensteinness are étale-local, giving singular locus equal to the image of the vertex line and canonical index one away from the origin. The quotient of that line has invariant ring k[t^m], hence is A1. Virtual-freeness preservation plus the product formula gives closed-point mld one on the entire line and smooth-point mld three off it. The non-klt locus is the line because the punctured line is étale-locally the product of the lc non-klt cone vertex with a smooth curve, the origin is non-klt by the source, and the complement is smooth.

value.rationale: The finding exposes a structural feature directly relevant to the failed index conjecture: the arbitrary canonical index is not spread over the non-klt locus but is concentrated at one point, while neighboring singular points on the same irreducible non-klt stratum are Gorenstein and have the identical closed-point mld value one. This separates the behaviors of singularity, non-klt locus, minimal log discrepancy, and canonical index in one explicit family, and shows that even fixing the entire local closed-point mld profile along the singular stratum does not prevent an arbitrarily large isolated index jump. It is therefore more than a normalization or bookkeeping check.
